title: Francis Ngannou added to MVP’s Rousey-Carano card in May
content:
Francis Ngannou, widely recognized as the lineal heavyweight champion of mixed martial arts, was added to the fight card for Most Valuable Promotion’s event on May 16, headlined by a bout between Ronda Rousey and Gina Carano.

Ngannou, 39, will fight Philipe Lins in a five-round affair, which will be broadcast on Netflix. Ngannou has not fought since October 2024, when he knocked out Renan Ferreira to become the PFL heavyweight champ. The bout marked his only MMA fight with PFL after he joined the organization in 2023 and then fought two high-profile boxing matches against Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

Ngannou joined the PFL after a seven-year run with the UFC, where he won the heavyweight title in 2021, defended it in 2022, then failed to receive a satisfactory new contract and became one of the sport’s biggest free agents ever. Having never relinquished his belt in competition, Ngannou maintains his status as the lineal heavyweight champion in the eyes of many fans and analysts, given the UFC’s standing as the sport’s premier promotion.

“While the world was busy talking, I was busy evolving,” Ngannou said in a statement Monday. “Silence shouldn’t be mistaken for absence — it’s the sound of a predator closing the distance. Stepping back into the cage isn’t just a return; it’s a reclamation.

“My return to MMA demanded a stage that matched the scale of my ambition, and partnering with MVP to bring this event to Netflix ensures the entire world is watching.”

On March 6, the PFL — which has undergone significant reorganizations in the past year — announced that Ngannou was no longer under contract with the promotion.

Lins, 40, will enter the bout with a record of 18-5. He last fought at UFC 299 in 2022, defeating Ion Cutelaba via unanimous decision in a light heavyweight affair. Lins has not fought at heavyweight since 2020, when he lost back-to-back fights to open his time in the UFC.

Prior to that, Lins won the 2018 PFL heavyweight tournament.

“Francis Ngannou is unequivocally the best heavyweight MMA fighter in the world and his addition creates star power on one card like never before seen in the sport,” Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, co-founders of MVP, said in a statement. “Francis is one of the most feared knockout artists the sport has ever seen, and his return to MMA instantly makes this a historic night.”
